The method is $O(1)$ per voxel evaluation, as it involves a fixed number of hash and noise calculations regardless of world size.
Performance depends heavily on the `QUALITY` setting.
Quality 0 is the fastest, using only hash functions.
Quality 1 and 2 involve FBM noise calculations, which are more expensive.
The method scales linearly with the number of voxels evaluated.
Quality 1 and 2 have limited vertical range (up to y=19) and fixed terrain height scales.
Leaf placement is heuristic and may not cover all tree shapes perfectly.
Use for real-time voxel worlds where performance is critical and deterministic generation is required.
Use Quality 0 for low-end devices or simple aesthetic effects.
Use Quality 1 or 2 for standard voxel games.
Do not use for large-scale, continuous terrain generation requiring infinite height or complex biome transitions without additional logic.
Do not use if high-fidelity, organic tree shapes are required beyond the heuristic leaves placement.
